issues: The scene combines the approach with the city's earlier rebuilding and fortification; keep the fortification as a prior state, not an event happening during the approach. The prohibited-inventions note correctly flags this chronology.
The source says the city was rebuilt, then clarifies it was only partly rebuilt (Alma 49:3); the summary's unqualified wording is imprecise.

The visual inference of showing all elements in one view is a reasonable composition choice, but the source does not specify their exact spatial arrangement beyond the army being by the borders and dirt cast around it.
The proposed Lamanite-side viewpoint for the chief captains is a reasonable visual inference, but their exact position and vantage point are unspecified.
The supplied source does not identify the chief captains’ exact location, so avoid placing them at Ammonihah as a certainty; the verses establish only that they did not attack there.

The preceding scene summarizes the Lamanites as prepared with thick skin garments, but its quoted narration includes only shields and breastplates; treat the summarized details as source-backed, not as additional narration.

The scene mostly tracks the supplied verses and keeps Moroni’s supposition retrospective. However, “The group marched toward Noah to battle, according to Moroni’s desires” overstates verse 15: the march and its cause are stated in verses 12–13, while verse 15 says this outcome was according to Moroni’s desires. The unnamed group is specifically the Lamanites or Amalickiahites in context, but the scene conservatively leaves them unnamed.

Narration excerpt from Alma 49:15 is contiguous and verbatim, but starts mid-sentence and conveys only the outcome, not that Moroni had supposed this would happen. The narration’s word count is within the limit.
Lehi's command of the city is explicit, but the verses do not state that he is physically present with the defenders as the Lamanite army approaches.

The Lamanites are listed as characters, but Alma 49:18–20 describes the fortifications and Nephite preparations, not Lamanites physically present in this scene. Their presence is supported only by the preceding verse's report that their armies were brought up.

The summary includes the army's return to Nephi and report to Amalickiah, while the scene's visual inference depicts only the flight into the wilderness; keep the later return and report out of the depicted moment.
